features.description: Initialize a coherent Muntin Mojo project for the verified stable toolchain and record the exact toolchain version.
acceptance: Project layout is valid for the verified stable Mojo toolchain.
The exact Mojo version used for verification is recorded in project documentation or canonical check output.
A clean repository user can discover the canonical verification commands from README/docs.
evidence: pixi run --frozen mojo --version -> 'Mojo 1.1.0 (8189361e)' (pixi 0.81.0); pixi.lock pins mojo-1.1.0 and mojo-compiler-1.1.0 for osx-arm64 and linux-64.
./scripts/check.sh -> exit 0; 'toolchain' step prints 'Mojo 1.1.0 (8189361e)' and fails on any other version; 'build package' step: mojo precompile --Werror src/muntin -> ok.
README.md 'Development' section lists ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh and git diff --check plus the Mojo version.

acceptance: scripts/check.sh exists, is executable, and returns nonzero on relevant build/static failures.
scripts/test.sh exists, is executable, and runs executable Muntin tests.
Both scripts exit 0 on the verified M0 implementation.
evidence: ./scripts/check.sh -> exit 0 (toolchain, format, architecture boundary, build package, build tests --Werror, build example).
./scripts/test.sh -> exit 0 (tests/test_app.mojo: 'Summary ... 6 tests run: 6 passed , 0 failed , 0 skipped').

Negative (planted then reverted): type error in src/muntin/http.mojo -> check.sh exit 1 at 'build package' ('cannot implicitly convert StringLiteral["x"] value to Int'); misformatted function -> check.sh exit 1 at 'format'; 'from flare.http import Request as FlareRequest' in app.mojo -> check.sh exit 1 at 'architecture boundary'; unused variable in a test -> check.sh exit 1 at 'build tests'.
Negative (planted then reverted): router condition replaced with 'if True:' -> test.sh exit 1 (3 FAIL); test file whose main() never runs TestSuite -> test.sh exit 1 ('ran no tests').

features.description: Implement the minimal Muntin-owned application contracts for request dispatch.
acceptance: Muntin owns the application entry point and Request/Response contracts or documented proven equivalents.
A handler can be registered and dispatched for a static GET route.
Muntin core/public modules do not import Flare.
evidence: src/muntin/{__init__,http,app}.mojo define Muntin-owned App, Request, Response; App.get[path](handler) registers a static GET route; App.handle(Request) -> Response dispatches.
./scripts/test.sh -> PASS test_get_hello_through_backend_seam (app.handle(Request("GET", "/hello")) -> 200 'hello').
./scripts/check_boundaries.sh (run by check.sh) -> 'ok: no Flare/socket imports in src/muntin'; planted Flare import and 'muntin_flare_adapter' identifier each -> exit 1.

features.description: Prove GET /hello returns status 200 and body hello through real Muntin routing/application dispatch.
acceptance: An executable test sends a GET /hello request through Muntin's application dispatch path.
The observed response status is 200.
The observed response body is hello.
The test does not bypass routing by calling the hello handler directly.
evidence: ./scripts/test.sh -> PASS test_get_hello_through_test_client (TestClient(app).get("/hello") -> status 200, text 'hello'), test_get_hello_through_backend_seam, test_router_selects_matching_route, test_unregistered_path_is_not_found, test_method_mismatch_is_not_found; 6 tests run: 6 passed.

Tests never call hello() directly; mutation 'if True:' in App.handle route matching -> 3 tests FAIL, test.sh exit 1. Independent reviewer mutations (ignore path, ignore method, 404->200, TestClient hardcoding 'hello') were each caught.

features.description: Prove transport replaceability with an in-memory/reference backend or TestClient.
acceptance: The application can be driven without opening a real network socket.
The same Muntin application seam intended for real backend adapters is exercised.
No public application API exposes or requires Flare types.
evidence: ./scripts/test.sh -> PASS test_get_hello_through_test_client: muntin.testing.TestClient builds a Muntin Request and calls App.handle, the documented backend seam (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 'Implemented M0 layout').
src/muntin/testing.mojo imports only .app and .http; check_boundaries.sh -> 'ok: no Flare/socket imports in src/muntin'.
Public exports (src/muntin/__init__.mojo): App, Request, Response only; none reference Flare.

features.description: Keep the M0 public surface compatible with Muntin's canonical DX direction without inventing unsupported Mojo syntax.
acceptance: The checked-in Hello World example/test uses only Muntin-owned application concepts.
Any deviation from a docs/DX.md target syntax caused by Mojo is documented with toolchain/compiler evidence.
M0 does not expose backend/runtime machinery merely to register an ordinary route.
evidence: main.mojo (Hello World) uses only muntin.App and muntin.testing.TestClient; check.sh 'build example' -> ok; ./build/muntin prints '200 hello'.
app.get["/hello"](hello), TestClient(app), client.get, response.status, response.text() and Response.text("ok", status=201) compile and run as in docs/DX.md (tests/test_app.mojo).

Mojo 1.1.0 limitation recorded in docs/DX.md 'Proven vs. target status': storing 'def() -> String' in a struct field -> "error: struct fields do not support trait types; 'def() -> String' is a trait"; Muntin stores 'def() thin -> String' internally, application handlers unchanged.
Registering a route requires no backend/runtime type: App.get takes only a route literal and a handler.

features.description: Finish M0 with accurate architecture, DX, and handoff state.
acceptance: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md matches the implemented dependency direction.
docs/DX.md clearly distinguishes proven syntax from future target syntax.
AGENT_PROGRESS.md records successful verification and the next work item.
git diff --check succeeds.

AGENT_PROGRESS.md records verification commands, decisions, limitations and next step (M1-001).

features.description: Heterogeneous handler shapes can share one App.
acceptance: An executable test registers def() -> String, def(Int) -> User, and def(Request) -> Response handlers in one app and dispatches each through handle(Request) -> Response.
Registration keeps the runtime handler value syntax app.get["/users/{id}"](get_user), or compiler evidence shows why it cannot.

Storage candidates (capturing closure, trampoline, function pointer + context, compile-time generated wrapper, type erasure, compile-time handler parameter) are compared with minimal reproductions and compiler output recorded in docs/DX.md.
evidence: ./scripts/test.sh -> exit 0; tests/test_spike_handler_model.mojo PASS test_heterogeneous_handler_shapes_share_one_app: RuntimeApp registers root() -> String (GET /), get_user(id: Int) -> User (GET /users/{id}), raw(req: Request) -> Response (POST /raw) via app.get["/"](root) / app.get["/users/{id}"](get_user) / app.post["/raw"](raw); handle(Request) returns 200, 200, 201, and 404 for GET /raw.
Runtime handler value syntax kept: handlers stored as Int address bits + same-type trampoline (one private generic _register), guarded by comptime assert size_of[F]() == size_of[Int]().

Closure repro (Mojo 1.1.0): storing a second capturing closure of identical signature in List[Route[type_of(a1)]] -> "cannot be converted from 'Route[def(s: String) -> String]' to 'Route[def(s: String) -> String]'"; field of type def(String) -> String -> "struct fields do not support trait types"; closure to thin -> "cannot implicitly convert 'def(s: String) -> String' value to 'def(String) thin -> String'". rebind -> 'rebind input type ... does not match result type'. Comparison table in docs/DX.md 'Handler model (M0.5 spike)'.
Fallback PASS test_compile_time_parameter_fallback_dispatches_same_shapes (app.get["/users/{id}", get_user]()); recorded as fallback only.
Mutation: String.to_response returning status 500 -> test_heterogeneous_handler_shapes_share_one_app FAIL.

features.description: A typed path handler can adapt to Request -> Response.
acceptance: GET /users/42 delivers Int(42) to def get_user(id: Int) through the app's dispatch, with no parsing in application code.
Invalid integer input produces a client error response instead of reaching the handler.
Whether a route/handler mismatch fails at compile time is demonstrated with compiler output.
evidence: ./scripts/test.sh -> PASS test_typed_path_handler_adapts_to_request_response: GET /users/42 -> 'User(42, Alice)' (segment parsed to Int by the trampoline, not by application code); GET /users/abc -> 400; GET /users -> 404.
Mutation: trampoline passing 0 instead of the parsed segment -> test_typed_path_handler_adapts_to_request_response FAIL.

Compile-time mismatch: app.get["/users/{id}"](root) fails to compile with 'note: call expansion failed' at the registration line and 'note: constraint failed: route declares path parameters but the handler takes none'.

features.description: A typed return value can convert to Response.
acceptance: String, a user-defined struct, and Response return values are each converted to a Response by one Muntin-owned mechanism.
No JSON serializer is introduced.
evidence: ./scripts/test.sh -> PASS test_typed_return_values_convert_to_response: String -> 200 'hello', User -> 'User(7, Alice)', Response -> 201 'raw:ping', all via trait ToResponse (to_response(self) -> Response).
String and Response conform via __extension String(ToResponse) / __extension Response(ToResponse); builds under ./scripts/check.sh (--Werror) -> exit 0. No JSON code added.
Mutation: String.to_response returning status 500 -> test_typed_return_values_convert_to_response FAIL.

features.description: Implement the Flare adapter behind the existing Muntin backend seam.
acceptance: Adapter depends inward on Muntin application contracts.
No application handler signature requires a Flare type.
Adapter contract tests pass.
Adapter contract tests convert a Flare Request to a Muntin Request, dispatch it through App.handle, and convert the Muntin Response back to a Flare Response without opening a socket.
CI installs the locked `flare` environment and ./scripts/check_flare.sh exits 0 on both Ubuntu and macOS runners.
evidence: Adapter adapters/flare/muntin_flare.mojo (outside src/; imports flare.http and muntin's public App/Request/Response only): MuntinHandler(Handler).serve converts, calls App.handle, converts back.

./scripts/check_flare.sh -> exit 0: adapters/flare/test_muntin_flare.mojo 7/7 (conversion, App.handle dispatch, 404 path/method, TestClient parity); adapters/flare/serve_probe.mojo builds with --Werror (HttpServer.serve accepts an owned MuntinHandler); adapter does not build in the default env.
CI on PR #5: flare job (cold locked install, check_flare.sh) passes on ubuntu-latest (ubuntu24) and macos-latest (macos26); verify job passes without the flare env.
Planted adapter mutations turn check_flare.sh red (list in AGENT_PROGRESS.md). ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, git diff --check -> exit 0.

features.description: Prove a real localhost HTTP round trip through Flare and Muntin.
acceptance: A real local HTTP request enters through Flare, crosses the Muntin adapter, dispatches a Muntin route, and returns the expected response.

Concretely: a real HTTP client sends GET /hello over a loopback TCP connection to Flare's HttpServer (bind/serve) serving MuntinHandler, which calls App.handle on an App whose GET /hello handler returns "hello"; the client observes status 200 and body exactly "hello".
The equivalent application behavior still passes through the in-memory backend: TestClient on the same App registration returns the same status and body.

The network test binds loopback only, does not race server readiness, bounds every wait, and leaves no server process behind; ./scripts/check_flare.sh runs it and passes in CI on both Ubuntu and macOS.
All M0 checks remain passing without weakening their intent.
evidence: adapters/flare/test_localhost_roundtrip.mojo: forked child runs HttpServer.bind(SocketAddr.localhost(0)).serve(MuntinHandler(hello_app())); parent's HttpClient GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/hello -> 200 'hello' (== TestClient(hello_app()).get("/hello")), GET /missing -> 404 'Not Found'. Readiness = bind (already listening); 5 s client timeouts; SIGKILL+waitpid in finally; child alarm(30).

./scripts/check_flare.sh -> exit 0: round trip 1/1 (wire: HTTP/1.1 200 'OK', Content-Length 5, no Content-Type), pgrep finds no leftover; default env cannot build it. CI flare job green on ubuntu-latest (ubuntu24) and macos-latest (macos26).
Planted mutations each turn it red (list in AGENT_PROGRESS.md), including bypassing App.handle and removing child cleanup.
./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, git diff --check -> exit 0; src/muntin unchanged.

features.description: Deliver one path parameter to a handler as Int without manual application parsing.
acceptance: The public syntax is proven to compile on the supported Mojo version and documented in docs/DX.md.
GET /users/42 yields handler input Int(42).
Invalid integer input produces documented client-error behavior.
The same handler signature works with in-memory and any enabled real backend.

Concretely: production muntin.App accepts app.get["/users/{id}"](get_user) with def get_user(id: Int) -> String, in the same App as existing def() -> String routes; the segment is converted to Int by Muntin before the handler is called, with no parsing or Request access in application code.

GET /users/abc (and other non-integer segments, including forms Mojo's Int(String) would accept such as +42, ' 42', 4_2) returns 400 'Bad Request' without invoking the handler; GET /users and paths with a different segment count or static segment return 404; a method mismatch returns 404; existing exact routes behave as in M0.
Binding is positional: a {name} segment is not checked against the handler parameter's name, and docs say so. A route whose {param} count does not match the handler fails to compile.

One App registering the typed route is driven through muntin.testing.TestClient and through a real loopback request to Flare's HttpServer serving MuntinHandler; both observe the same status and body for an integer path whose handler output differs from the raw segment (e.g. /users/042 -> '42') and for /users/abc -> 400. Routing and extraction live in Muntin; the adapter is not changed to understand {id}.

Any handler-storage mechanism is safe or, if unsafe, private, justified and contained; the choice and alternatives are recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. ./scripts/check.sh, ./scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/check_flare.sh pass locally and in CI on Ubuntu and macOS.
evidence: src/muntin/app.mojo: App.get overloaded on def() thin -> String and def(Int) thin -> String, stored as a Variant (no unsafe code); App.handle matches {name} segments and converts to Int (optional '-', ASCII digits, Int range) before calling the handler, else 400.

./scripts/test.sh -> exit 0: tests/test_app.mojo 13/13 (/users/42 -> '42', /users/042 -> '42', +42/' 42'/4_2/abc/overflow -> 400 'Bad Request', /users, /users/, /user/42, POST -> 404, exact routes unchanged, first registered match wins). ./scripts/check.sh -> exit 0: 6 tests/compile_fail fixtures rejected with their expected 'constraint failed' text (arity, malformed literal).

./scripts/check_flare.sh -> exit 0: adapters/flare/test_localhost_roundtrip.mojo 2/2; one App with /hello and /users/{id} over loopback through Flare HttpServer + unchanged MuntinHandler gives /users/42 -> 200 '42', /users/042 -> '42', /users/abc -> 400, /users -> 404, each equal to TestClient; no leftover process. CI verify + flare green on ubuntu-latest (ubuntu24) and macos-latest (macos26).
Planted mutations each turned a check red (list in AGENT_PROGRESS.md); fresh-context review found no material issue; git diff --check clean.
